correctness.rationale: For fixed four-color successor-contact rule, the support pair (S,T) has 15×15=225 possibilities and evolves autonomously. Support cardinalities never increase; along a support cycle the transition maps are bijective, and surjective labelings prevent shorter periods than the induced return-color permutation. An independent 225-state full enumeration gave exactly 25 recurrent masks and the seven rows (period,|S|,|T|;count): (1,1,1;8),(1,1,2;4),(1,2,1;4),(1,2,2;2),(4,2,2;2),(4,4,4;1),(6,3,3;4). Multiplication by U_j(n)=j! S(n,j) yields P1=8+4U2(a)+4U2(b)+2U2(a)U2(b), P4=2U2(a)U2(b)+U4(a)U4(b), P6=4U3(a)U3(b). This finite support enumeration is exhaustive for any a,b>=1, unlike small-graph enumeration. Orbit counts divide by respective periods.
residual_risks: No transient-entry time or basin counts; labelled graph checks alone do not prove the universal claim, whereas support quotient exhaustiveness does.

value.rationale: A complete exact recurrence classification over every labelled complete bipartite graph at four colors is a natural extension beyond the standard 3-color case. The primitive six-cycle family and exact emergence threshold a,b>=3 are mathematically nontrivial, and the 225-state support quotient makes an infinite graph-family classification tractable.
residual_risks: Classification applies only to contact-threshold-one synchronous four-color dynamics and bicliques, not general graphs.

limitations: No transient bounds, basins, other graph families or palette sizes.
